userStories.title: Service worker update lifecycle: prompt user to refresh on new deployment
userStories.description: When a new version of the app is deployed to Vercel, the existing service worker continues serving the stale cached version to users who have the PWA open. Without a skipWaiting and clients.claim flow plus a UI prompt, users may run outdated JavaScript for hours or days. This is especially risky after order-flow or admin changes.
acceptanceCriteria: The new service worker calls skipWaiting() inside its install event when a SKIP_WAITING message is received
The service worker registration in the app detects the 'waiting' state (new SW available)
A non-intrusive toast/banner appears at the top of the page: 'Update available — tap to refresh'
Clicking the refresh button sends the SKIP_WAITING message to the waiting SW, then calls window.location.reload()
The update check is performed on every page focus event (visibilitychange) in addition to the initial registration
Admin and KDS routes show the update banner with higher priority (immediate, not dismissible without refreshing)
technicalNotes: Pattern: registration.waiting.postMessage({ type: 'SKIP_WAITING' }) in the client; self.addEventListener('message', e => { if (e.data.type === 'SKIP_WAITING') self.skipWaiting(); }) in sw.js
Use navigator.serviceWorker.addEventListener('controllerchange', ...) to detect when the new SW has taken control, then reload
Reference: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/workbox/handling-service-worker-updates/
Next.js Turbopack builds change the SW file hash on each deploy — the browser detects the changed sw.js and triggers the update flow automatically

userStories.title: Security response headers via Next.js middleware

Reference: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/headers
